title: A Spacecraft Launched in 2018 Reaches Mercury This November

scenes.text: This spacecraft left Earth in 2018 and reaches Mercury in November.
The trip took nine gravity-assist flybys: one past Earth, two past Venus, six past Mercury.
It was due last year. Then a thruster glitch left its engines too weak to brake into orbit.
So engineers rerouted the whole trip. The new orbit burn is set for November 21st.
It's a European and Japanese mission with two orbiters, costing about 1.65 billion euros.
Launched in 2018. Arriving in November. Eight years for one braking burn.

description:
ESA and JAXA's BepiColombo launched in October 2018 and is now set to enter orbit around Mercury on 21 November 2026.
A thruster problem delayed the original December 2025 arrival, so engineers redesigned the final approach. The mission carries two orbiters and was estimated at about 1.65 billion euros.
Would you want to be on the team that has to nail that engine burn?
first_comment: Mercury is the planet closest to the Sun and the least explored of the rocky ones. What would you most want BepiColombo to find?
